text:
Maria G.: FYI — nightly perf job spikes OOMs on longctx pools for seqlen 8192+. Started after PR #4821 merged (kv warmup + eviction tweak). Repro ~30% on canary.

Jordan: ugh. Which nodes are failing? any kernel-routing changes in that PR?

Maria G.: failing on gpu-pool-4a and gpu-pool-4b. PR changed eviction anneal + added a fastpath that can prefer compacted slabs for warmup; diff: https://stash/redwood/4821

Sam K.: can you paste the OOM log? suspect fragmentation rather than raw alloc ceiling.

Maria G.: pasted minimal log: 
``` 
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] worker-17 ERR alloc failed: requested 246MiB but only 184MiB available in slablet
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] worker-17 INFO kv: eviction_candidate_count=1024 slab_frag=0.61 warmup_hits=9
[2026-03-17T02:12:14Z] worker-17 panic: runtime: out of memory
``` 

Priya: warmup_hits low, eviction_candidate_count large — sounds like the anneal made eviction less aggressive for certain stride patterns. Could fragment slabs if warmup prefers moving small entries around.

Sam K.: I profiled one failed trace — flame shows a lot of small copies in kv-copy hotpath, and kernel routing landed on the mmap-backed slow allocator for many longctx requests. Looks like the kernel-selection heuristic favors compacted-slab kernel for seqlen < 4096, but warmup changed distribution so we misroute 8k tokens to the slower path. Snip from pprof: `kv_copy -> compact_move -> memcpy` high p99.

Jordan: that's consistent with the allocation log. Any bisect results?

Maria G.: ran quick git-bisect against main-ish; culprit tippoints to commit 0f3a7b4 (author: @nate) — the anneal param change + condition in kernel_router.go. Reverting that commit locally removes OOMs in 100% of repro runs.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-17T01:50:00Z for ref 0f3a7b4 detected. Rollout progress: 70% -> paused by eng-runtime.

Priya: +1 to hold rollout. We should revert 0f3a7b4 on main and put a rollout-hold until we have a patch. 

Sam K.: propose quick mitigation: 1) revert anneal threshold to previous value, 2) tighten kernel routing rule to route seqlen >= 6144 to the legacy allocator, 3) add a short-term metric to count `seqlen_misroute` on p99. I can ship a revert PR and a follow-up gating PR.

Maria G.: SG. I can open the revert now and start a ~1h soak test on gpu-pool-4. Also will add a stress job that ramps seqlen distribution to catch this earlier.

Jordan: once revert is in, can ops un-pause and resume rollout with canary at 10% and trace for 24h? we need to ensure no perf cliff.

Priya: add regression test to CI harness that runs longctx workload (8192 tokens) in a tiny VM to catch fragmentation patterns — maybe lower mem cap so it fails fast.

Sam K.: noted. I'll also add the pprof flame sample collector to nightly and a CI check that p99 small-copy time doesn't regress >20%.

Maria G.: created revert PR https://stash/redwood/commit/revert-0f3a7b4 and rerun canary. Initial soak (10 runs) - zero OOMs so far. Will update in 30m. :thumbsup:

Jordan: thanks. Once soak stable, coordinate with release to ship revert and then schedule a careful redesign of anneal+routing (need unit tests for stride patterns).

Priya: logging action items: Maria -> soak + CI test, Sam -> routing tweak + pprof, Jordan -> coordinate rollback release, Priya -> add stress-case.

Maria G.: noted. tagging @eng-sre for follow-up after revert.
